deepdive.sec: Mining Consumables & Mineral-Processing Equipment (picks-and-shovels to global mining)

bull_bear.body:
- Major leverage event: ~$838m Molycop debt + INR1,500 cr parent acquisition debt (Std Chartered/Axis/EXIM) on top of INR1,700 cr already raised. Molycop debt already paid down ~$220m (from ~$1,050m to $838m) pre-close.
- Stated priority: deleverage to ~3x within 3-4 years via revenue + cost synergies + non-core asset sales.
- Working capital improved FY26 (better collections + payables); DSO target 100-105 days.
- Capex self-funded from internal accruals + existing facilities.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Consumables execution credibility:** flat FY26 vs repeated 15% guidance (FY24 10%, FY25 11%) — analyst pushback; "timing/logistics" narrative must convert to H1 FY27 revenue (the swing item).
- **Logistics / Middle-East shipping:** vessel + container shortage stranded FG; finding alternate routes but a recurring geopolitical exposure.
- **Molycop integration & leverage:** ~$838m+ debt; only 1 month consol in Q1; ~$30m more one-time transaction cost hits Q1 FY27 P&L; FY-end alignment Jun→Mar adds reporting noise.
- **Molycop growth deferral:** Cobre Panama + Grasberg restarts pushed to FY28 → only ~3% FY27 growth; volume/market-share not disclosed (transparency gap).
- **Chile regulatory slippage:** commercial production approval-gated; revenue could push to FY28.
- **Commodity/steel pricing:** Molycop revenue is steel-conversion linked; RM volatility on Tega consumables.
- **Equipment lumpiness:** project execution swings (H1 +65 / H2 flat) — single-order dependent (NMDC).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Detailed, multi-speaker (group + Molycop CFO/COO on call) — good transparency on the deal mechanics (debt, transaction costs, synergy framework, 100/200-day plans). However, somewhat defensive on the repeated consumables miss — declined to cut the 15% guidance despite three soft years, leaning on "cyclicality" and a logistics one-off. Pushed back accurately on an analyst conflating the $30m transaction cost with an operating "loss." Declined to share Molycop volume/market-share data. Overall credible but the consumables guidance now carries a show-me burden.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- This is a re-platforming quarter: post-Molycop, Tega goes from a ~INR1,770 cr Indian consumables/equipment maker to a >~$1.7bn global mining-solutions platform — but FY27 reported numbers will be messy (1-month Molycop consol, ~$30m one-time Q1 cost, FY-end migration, lower blended margin).
- The "flat consumables" is the real debate, not Molycop: order book +18% and ~INR100 cr of deferred revenue support the timing story, but it's the third consecutive year below the 15% line — H1 FY27 execution is the single most important verification item.
- Molycop is a steel-linked, capex-light, ~12%-margin cash cow bought largely with debt — the thesis is deleveraging + synergy capture, not organic growth (only ~3% FY27).
- Tega is a leveraged play on the copper/gold mining-capex supercycle: it sells the picks-and-shovels (liners, grinding media, beneficiation plants) into electrification-driven copper demand — a derivative "Grid-Capex / energy-transition" beneficiary one layer removed.
- Chile plant + Japanese-collaboration equipment product are FY27/FY28 optionality, both back-end loaded (Q3-Q4).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Among the leading global suppliers of mill and wear liners, and one of the leading global producers of polymer-based mill liners, with brand presence built since 1976 and customers across more than 92 countries
- Global manufacturing and service network located close to major mining regions, giving customer proximity, supply-chain responsiveness and faster technical support
- R&D centres in India and Chile focused on smart IT-enabled products, ESG-aligned solutions and recycling systems supporting a circular economy, with collaboration with technical institutes
- Strong aftermarket business model with a diversified customer base across commodities and geographies
- Comprehensive lifecycle equipment management with smart monitoring and predictive maintenance that reduces unexpected downtime and extends equipment life for mining customers
- Ability to generally pass on cost increases to customers with a lag of one to two quarters, with pricing inputs reviewed monthly to support dynamic pricing
- Tega Industries Business Excellence Model (TIBEM) and TQM deployment driving productivity, cost, delivery and quality; Industry 4.0 digital twin and IIoT deployment at the Dahej plant
- The Molycop acquisition adds market-leading grinding media, process control and analytics, creating an integrated one-stop mill optimisation offering across the comminution circuit
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity and raw material price risk — Volatility in raw material prices and supply disruptions from geopolitical or market developments may increase procurement costs and impact working capital. The Company generally passes on cost increases to customers only with a lag of one to two quarters, so margin pressure is not immediately recoverable; the Middle East crisis and the prolonged Ukraine-Russia war disrupted global supply chains and raw material availability during FY 2025-26.
- Geographic and geopolitical concentration risk — Exposure to different economic conditions, regulatory changes, political instability or natural disasters across India, South America, North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Africa may affect business continuity and revenue. Exports constituted approximately 84% of standalone turnover and the Company serves customers across 92 countries, making it structurally exposed to cross-border conditions and currency.
- Operational and capacity risk — Capacity constraints, inefficient utilisation of plant facilities or inadequate preparedness for natural or man-made disruptions may affect production schedules and operational continuity. Product failures could also impact customer confidence and market position.
- Competitor risk in mining consumables — Intensifying competition in the mining consumables sector may affect market share, growth prospects and profitability, requiring continuous investment in product development, innovation and market expansion to defend the polymer-based mill liner position.
- Supply chain and logistics dependence — Dependence on external logistics providers and suppliers may lead to delays, cost increases and disruptions in product delivery. Logistical challenges impacted the Company heavily at the year end.
- Project execution risk — Limited project management capability may lead to delays, cost overruns and inefficient project delivery - material given the ongoing Chile greenfield build, brownfield expansions and the integration of the acquired Molycop business.
- Financial risk from inflation, interest rates and leverage — Inflation and rising interest rates may increase borrowing costs and affect profitability; market volatility or insufficient insurance coverage may affect financial stability. The Rs 1,500 Crore debt facility raised to fund the Molycop acquisition makes deleveraging a stated commitment.
- Technology and cybersecurity risk — Outdated systems, technological disruptions or cybersecurity incidents may affect operations, decision-making processes and customer confidence; the Company maintains cyber risk insurance covering losses from security breaches, electronic theft, communications disruption or cyber vandalism.
- Human resource and succession risk — Challenges in attracting or retaining skilled talent may affect operational performance and long-term growth, and inadequate succession planning may create leadership gaps.
- Intellectual property infringement risk — Unauthorised use of patented technologies may lead to legal disputes and potential revenue loss - structurally significant for a business whose moat rests on proprietary liner design and material technology.
- Health and safety risk — Failure to adhere to safety standards may result in near-miss incidents, injuries or fatalities, affecting the Company's safety record, reputation and ability to secure business opportunities from mining customers.
- Compliance risk — Non-compliance with regulatory requirements across the multiple jurisdictions in which the Company operates may lead to legal penalties, operational disruptions and reputational damage.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Consumables (~84% of rev, FY26 flat):** mill liners / wear solutions / screens / spares & conversion; bespoke, design-led, 3-6 month order-to-revenue lag. FY26 weakness attributed to (a) orders bunching into Feb-Mar and (b) Middle-East shipping disruption (no vessel/container availability) stranding FG. Q4 consumables rev INR440.6 cr (vs INR456.8 cr, -INR16.2 cr). Normalised Q4 consumables EBITDA margin ~27.7% (adding back INR776 mn one-off).
- **Equipment / Tega McNally Minerals (~16%, +25% FY26):** dense-media/mineral-beneficiation plants & project equipment (NMDC-type). H1 +65.4% then H2 flat on project-execution timing (depends on customer site readiness). EBITDA margin 12-13%.
- **Molycop (acquired 01-Jun-26, with Apollo Funds minority):** global grinding-media (high-chrome + forged balls) for mining comminution; ~$1,539m FY26 (Jun-end) revenue, ~12% EBITDA, ~1% growth; capex-light (~2-3% of revenue). Mgmt declined to disclose volume split (high-chrome vs forged) or market share for now. Consolidates from 01-Jun (1 month in Q1 FY27); FY-end migrating Jun→Mar.

business.body: Tega designs and manufactures wear-resistant mining consumables - polymer-based mill and wear liners, screens, trommels, chute liners, hydrocyclones and conveyor products - together with mineral processing equipment such as crushers, vibrating screens, feeders, thickeners, pumps and filter presses through its subsidiary Tega McNally Minerals. Its products protect and improve grinding and mineral beneficiation circuits for mining and bulk material handling customers, supported by a strong aftermarket replacement-consumables model. Customers span steel, power, cement, iron ore, copper, zinc, aluminium, gold, platinum and aggregates, with exports constituting approximately 84% of standalone turnover.

- **Copper/gold supercycle pull-through:** mgmt framed structural demand — gold demand >5,000t (2025 record, supply +~1%/yr); copper demand +3%/yr vs supply +2%, +40% by 2040 needing ~$250bn and ~80 new mines → more mining capex = more consumables/grinding-media/equipment demand.
- **Chile plant:** new consumables capacity nearshoring to Latin-American copper belt (commission Q3 FY27).
- **New equipment product** (Japanese collaboration, aggregate business, Q3 FY27) — forward revenue optionality.
- **Geographic equipment expansion:** Canada, CIS, Middle-East beneficiation exports.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Integrate Molycop as the first strategic priority - management has set clear priorities for the first eight quarters: combine complementary strengths, align capabilities and systems, enhance customer value, support innovation and build a platform for long-term growth
- Evolve from a specialist consumables supplier into one of the world's leading designers and manufacturers of critical-to-operate consumables across multiple stages of the mineral processing value chain
- Offer an integrated one-stop mill optimisation solution by combining Molycop's grinding media, process control and analytics with Tega's mill lining systems, screening media and specialised consumables
- Pursue a multi-pronged capacity expansion strategy across geographies - the new Chile manufacturing facility plus brownfield expansions across existing plants to enhance throughput and utilisation
- Deepen customer partnerships, strengthen innovation capabilities and execute with discipline across global operations
- Deleverage debt from present levels following the acquisition financing
- Prioritise in-house manufacturing to retain control over cost, delivery and quality, using structured due diligence where external sourcing is required
- Digitalise products and manufacturing through IIoT, sensors, integrated ERP/MES and digital dashboards, with a digital twin deployed at Dahej
- Drive operational excellence through the Tega Industries Business Excellence Model (TIBEM) and Total Quality Management across productivity, cost, delivery and quality
- Advance the SAVE framework (Sustainably Adding Value through Engineering) across decarbonisation, resource optimisation and circularity, including a dedicated facility for processing end-of-life mill liners to recover rubber and metal
- Strengthen supply chain resilience through an expanded vendor network, product-based manufacturing allocation across plants and a Business Continuity Plan
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 Tega advanced a multi-pronged capacity expansion strategy across geographies to address increasing demand. The key development was construction of a new manufacturing facility in Chile, described as going on in full swing and required to support projected growth in Latin America; the facility is expected to commence commercial production in FY 2026-27 and will serve key Latin American mining markets including Chile, Peru, Brazil and Argentina. In parallel the Company undertook brownfield expansions across existing plants to enhance throughput and capacity utilisation, and pursued operational efficiency through capacity augmentation, automation and structured process improvements under the Tega Industries Business Excellence Model (TIBEM). Digital integration across manufacturing supported real-time visibility and predictive maintenance, with an Industry 4.0 deployment at the Dahej plant covering a digital twin of manufacturing processes, IIoT-connected machines and real-time monitoring and control. The Company states it expands production capacity once utilisation reaches defined thresholds and demand visibility is established. Separately, the acquisition of Molycop - announced on September 10, 2025 and completed on June 1, 2026 in consortium with funds managed by affiliates of Apollo at an enterprise value of approximately USD 1.5 billion - adds Molycop's 13 manufacturing facilities and 2 joint ventures, substantially expanding the combined manufacturing footprint across the United States, Canada, Latin America and Australia. The acquisition was financed through a Rs 1,713 Crore preferential equity issuance and a Rs 1,500 Crore debt facility arranged from Standard Chartered Bank and certain other banks and financial institutions. On the sustainability side the Company plans expansion of rooftop solar capacity to 1 MWp by 2027 and the development of a dedicated facility for processing end-of-life mill liners to recover rubber and metal components. As at March 31, 2026 the Company had 3 plants and 18 offices in India; international operations are carried out through subsidiary companies.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Long-term demand fundamentals in the global mining sector remain favourable, supported by a diversified customer base, a strong aftermarket business model and the Molycop acquisition
- Growing global demand for copper driven by electrification, renewable energy infrastructure and electric vehicles is supporting increased mining activity and higher demand for mineral processing consumables
- Gold and copper are markets characterised by structural scarcity - global gold demand reached a record 5,000 tonnes in 2025 while supply grew only 1%, and 2025 copper demand growth of ~3% outpaced ~1% mine supply growth amid declining ore grades and mine disruptions
- UNCTAD projects copper demand will increase by more than 40% by 2040, requiring approximately USD 250 billion in investment and nearly 80 new mines by 2030 - projects that can take up to 25 years to develop; this emerging supply gap is already lifting exploration budgets across Latin America, North America and Africa
- The global mill liners market was valued at $2.83 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $2.97 billion in 2026 and $4.59 billion by 2034; the metals, mining and minerals segment accounted for 50.17% of the market in 2026
- Poly-met (composite) mill liners are gaining increasing adoption across grinding applications on durability, lighter weight and operational efficiency
- Mining companies including BHP, Rio Tinto and Anglo American have announced multi-year investment pipelines focused on copper, iron ore and energy transition metals, accelerating global mining investment
- Declining ore grades in mature mining regions require more intensive crushing, grinding and mineral separation, driving demand for advanced milling systems, wear-resistant liners and process optimisation
- The Equipment business is more India-centric in customer base and execution footprint and grew approximately 25% year-on-year, while Consumables revenue was flat; domestic demand momentum is a key offset to uncertain global conditions
- Middle East crisis, the prolonged Ukraine-Russia war and logistical challenges disrupted global supply chains and raw material availability, weighing heavily at the year end
- Rising exploration investments and increased mineral production across major mining regions create favourable opportunities for advanced consumables and mineral processing technologies
- Global mining market is forecast to grow from USD 2.16 trillion in 2026 to USD 2.76 trillion in 2030, a CAGR of 6.3%
- The Company's order book grew by a strong 17% year-on-year, driven by healthy customer capex and maintenance spending on the back of a buoyant gold and copper commodity cycle
- Consumables division revenue remained flat but order booking remains very good
- The Company continues to make focused efforts to accelerate its growth trajectory in Q1 Financial Year 2026-27, supported by a healthy order pipeline and operational improvements

deepdive.thesis: Tega closed FY26 a transformational quarter behind: consolidated revenue INR1,774 cr (+5% YoY) with 22% adjusted EBITDA, but the headline is the 01-Jun-2026 completion of the Molycop grinding-media acquisition (with Apollo Funds), which roughly triples group scale (Molycop ~$1.54bn revenue) and adds ~$838m of debt — making FY27 a deleveraging-and-integration year. The core Tega consumables book disappointed (full-year flat vs 15% guidance) but management insists it is a logistics/timing slip (Middle-East vessel/container disruption stranded ~INR50 cr of finished goods; order book +18% YoY, ~INR906 cr executable in 12m), not lost share — so H1 FY27 execution is the key thing to verify.
